## Objective
- Update Brickline Dash into a playable swipe-controlled runner with directional character facing, stumble/death collision behavior, background music, and temporary surfboard power-ups.

## Requirements
- Swipe left/right to change lanes, swipe up to jump, and swipe down to slide.
- A mistimed jump into a small obstacle can cause a stumble and randomly remove one arm or leg; hitting an obstacle without avoiding it should end the run.
- Character face should face the movement direction.
- Add background music and collectible surfboards activated by touching the screen.

## Decisions
- Surfboards are collectible in the track and activated by tapping the screen or the board button; an active board lasts eight seconds.
- Background music is synthesized with Web Audio rather than using an external audio asset.
- A small crate/barrier collision early in a jump triggers a stumble; other unsafe collisions end the run.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added canvas swipe input for all four directions and updated the menu hint in `index.html`.
- Added surfboard pickups, an activation button, temporary board visuals, and synthesized background music in `game.js`.

- Check responsive presentation and run the game to catch runtime or syntax errors.

### Blocked
- (none)

1. Inspect and repair the current changes in `game.js`; verify all new state, callbacks, and update loops work together.
2. Ensure collision detection distinguishes an obstacle successfully avoided by a swipe from an unavoidable hit, while preserving the requested early-jump stumble case.
3. Improve/verify face orientation follows the runner’s actual movement direction.
4. Run the game and check the UI, controls, audio, and surfboard behavior; capture a screenshot if possible.

## Relevant Files
- `game.js`: Existing Three.js game and the main location of gameplay/input/audio changes.
- `index.html`: Updated control hint and new surfboard/swipe UI elements.
- `style.css`: Added styles for surfboard activation and swipe tip.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; no tests or browser verification have been run.
- Current collision code sets `o.resolved=true` on contact, consumes the board on any collision, stumbles for early jump collisions with crates/barriers, and otherwise calls `endRun()`.
- The current face rotation uses lane-target offset rather than verified actual movement direction.

## Objective
- Update Brickline Dash into a playable swipe-controlled runner with directional character facing, stumble/death collision behavior, synthesized background music, and collectible temporary surfboards.

## Requirements
- Swipe left/right to change lanes, up to jump, and down to slide.
- A mistimed jump into a small obstacle can cause a stumble and randomly remove one arm or leg; an unavoided obstacle hit ends the run.
- Character face should face the movement direction.
- Add background music and collectible surfboards activated by touching the screen.

## Decisions
- Surfboards are collected from the track and activated by tapping the screen or board button; an active board lasts eight seconds.
- Background music is synthesized with Web Audio rather than using an external audio asset.
- An early jump collision with a crate or barrier causes a stumble; other unsafe collisions end the run.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added swipe controls, surfboard pickups and activation, synthesized music, stumble visuals, and lateral-facing animation.
- Fixed surfboard pickup collision to check the runner’s interpolated lane position.
- Added a reset for surfboard readiness, button text, board visibility, and pending swipe input when starting a new run.
- Earlier JavaScript syntax and `git diff --check` passed; desktop/mobile smoke test reported no browser errors.

### Active
- Validate detailed gameplay behavior, including collision outcomes, stumble recovery, character-facing direction, audio toggle, surfboard lifecycle, and mobile controls.
- A browser validation script is in `/tmp/opencode/brickline-validate.mjs`; it was updated after an initial run failed due to test setup referencing inaccessible module-scoped variables. The revised script has not yet been rerun.

### Blocked
- `playwright-cli` cannot launch because its expected Chromium installation is missing; direct Playwright with `/usr/bin/google-chrome` worked for the earlier smoke test.

## Next Move
1. Rerun `node /tmp/opencode/brickline-validate.mjs` and inspect results; repair test hooks if needed.
2. Fix any gameplay issues surfaced, especially collision timing, facing, and surfboard pickup/expiry.
3. Re-run JavaScript syntax and `git diff --check`; confirm final uncommitted changes.

## Relevant Files
- `game.js`: Gameplay, controls, collisions, audio, character facing, and surfboard logic.
- `index.html`: Game UI, control hints, and surfboard activation button.
- `style.css`: Layout, responsive styling, and control presentation.
- `/tmp/opencode/brickline-validate.mjs`: In-progress browser validation script.
- `/tmp/opencode/brickline-menu.jpg`: Earlier menu smoke-test screenshot.
- `/tmp/opencode/brickline-run.jpg`: Earlier run smoke-test screenshot.
- `/tmp/opencode/brickline-mobile.jpg`: Earlier mobile smoke-test screenshot.

## Important Context
- Changes to `game.js`, `index.html`, and `style.css` are uncommitted.
- Earlier smoke test used Playwright with `/usr/bin/google-chrome`; HUD appeared during play and no JavaScript or console errors were reported.
- The initial detailed validation attempt failed with `ReferenceError: runnerRoot is not defined` in the test harness; the harness was then revised but not rerun.
